newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIANS AIM TO END NORTH AMERICAN SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIANS AIM TO END NORTH AMERICAN SUPREMACY.

text.p: Russians Alexei Urmanov and Ilya Kulik showed their determination to outclass the powerful North Americans as the world figure skating championships began with men's qualifying on Sunday.
Urmanov, Olympic and European champion, and former European winner Kulik both landed huge quadruple jumps that defending champion Todd Eldredge and Elvis Stojko could not equal.
American Eldredge, seeking a repeat title match the pair that Canadian Stojko won ahead of him, crashed to the ice on a triple axel, although he achieved one in combination with a triple toe loop.
But he did not attempt a quad, largely because he sprained his right ankle in training 10 days ago.

Stojko, who completed the first-ever quadruple toe loop-triple toe loop jump combination in the Champions Series final in Canada early this month, tried the quad alone on Sunday and fell on the landing.
The American beat the Canadian with former European champion Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine third in the opening group.
Urmanov won the second group from Kulik with Frenchman Eric Millot third.
The men's short programme worth one-third of the marks is on Wednesday with the free skating final on Thursday.

North Americans have won the last four crowns, Kurt Browning of Canada taking the title in 1993. Ukrainian Viktor Petrenko, then skating for the CIS Independent States), won in 1992 a year after the old Soviet Union broke up.
Urmanov's quad was a classic, a soaring effort that he landed cleanly and right in tune with a heavy beat from his music. "It looks easy but the last two practices it was a problem for me," he said.
He did the jump regularly as a teenager but stopped it after breaking a leg in the summer of 1992.
He earned the best marks of the day, four of 5.9 for technique and six of 5.9 for artistry from the seven judges.
Kulik improved considerably on his qualifying display at the European championships in January, when he was fourth with a poor display.
He said the qualifying still felt like a practice. "I wasn't nervous but I will be in the main event and then I'll be sharper," he said.

Eldredge and Stojko, who both did seven successful triples, had similar explanations for their misses. "I was feeling a little tired and I pulled it a little too hard," the American said. "But I wasn't favouring the ankle. Since yesterday it has felt 90 percent fine."

Stojko said of his quad attempt: "I went into it a little too fast and I was too anxious to get it around. But the set-up was nice and I felt fine going into it so we are in good shape for later in the week."
